chunks: Ibn Mahbub from al-Ala' ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the apostate, so he said: 'Whoever shows preference for a religion other than Islam and disbelieves in what Allah revealed to Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) after his Islam, there is no repentance for him, and his execution becomes obligatory, and his wife is separated from him, and what he leaves is divided among his children.'
ai.seo_question: What are the legal consequences for an apostate in Shia jurisprudence according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from Imam al-Baqir (AS), the concept of apostasy is defined specifically as rejecting the revelation given to Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) after one's initial conversion, distinguishing it from mere doubt. The ruling establishes that such a person is denied the usual window for repentance, resulting in obligatory execution, immediate dissolution of marriage, and inheritance passing exclusively to their children, reflecting the Shia jurisprudential view on the status of the murtadd's estate.
